req_desc:
Run manifest and health
/app/run.json installs, builds and serves the app on port 4173 or APP_PUBLIC_PORT, and the health path answers as stated in Deployment.

Seeded sign-in and sessions
The seeded broker, beekeepers and growers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie that every desk request uses, as specified in API.

One error order and shape
Every API error uses the single error body and the single precedence order stated in API.

Server boundary
The server accepts only same-origin writes, enforces the body limits, never serves source or credentials, and starts and stays healthy when Kill Bill, Mailpit or MinIO is unreachable, as qualified in Server boundary.

Real providers and env credentials
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment at start, never hard-coded or sent to the browser, and every invoice, email and stored file is a real record in Kill Bill, Mailpit or MinIO.

Three-viewport layout
The sign-in, desk, drop and inspection screens fit 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 with no horizontal overflow, arranged as described in Screens and layout.

Plat-map look
The desk reads as a survey plat on paper, with hairline block polygons, serif headings, monospace figures and one warm accent reserved for pay tiers.

Keyboard and focus
Every control is reachable in the stated Tab order, dialogs hold focus, Escape closes them and focus returns to the control that opened them.

Announced feedback
Every async action shows and announces its pending, success, field-error and outage copy from Feedback states in the named live regions, with an error summary that links to its fields.

Contrast and tap targets
Text and non-text elements meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast and every control is at least 44 by 44 pixels.

Orchards and blocks
The broker creates an orchard for a grower with its named blocks and acres, validated as stated in API.

Draft orders and season rules
The broker drafts an order for an orchard with hives per block and Pacific bloom and delivery dates, and the order takes the pay rules in effect on its bloom start date.

Opening an order invoices the deposit
Opening a draft order makes it visible to beekeepers and the grower and records one deposit invoice on the grower's Kill Bill account, or leaves it a draft with a 503 when billing is unreachable.

Cancelling an order
The broker cancels a draft, open or filled order with no delivered drops and its deposit invoice is voided, as qualified in Business rules; every other cancel is refused with 409.

Broker sets up a season order
In the browser the broker creates an orchard, drafts its order and opens it, and the desk shows the new order's plat map and ledger.

Beekeeper order view
Beekeepers see open orders and their own drops with their per-hive pay by tier, and never the grower's price, the commission or other beekeepers' drops.

Last-hive commit race
Committed hives never exceed hives ordered: simultaneous truckload commits are decided one at a time, so of two commits for the last open hives exactly one wins and the other gets 409 with the remaining count.

Beekeeper commits a truckload
In the browser a beekeeper commits a truckload to an open order, sees the ledger's open count fall, and sees the refusal copy with the remaining count when too few hives are left.

Pacific delivery date
A drop's delivery date is the America/Los_Angeles calendar date of its delivery time, and a drop dated after the order's delivery deadline is refused with 422.

Block room on delivery
A drop is logged into one block of its order, and a drop that would put more hives in a block than the block ordered is refused with 422.

Own drops only
A beekeeper can read, deliver, accept or dispute only their own drops and photos, and any other drop or photo id answers 404.

Beekeeper logs a drop
In the browser a beekeeper logs a committed truckload into a block with its Pacific date and time, and the drop and the block's delivered count update on screen.

Marking an order placed
The broker marks a filled order placed once every drop is delivered, and any other attempt is refused with 409.

Placement confirmation email
Marking an order placed sends the grower exactly one placement confirmation listing each block's hives and delivery date and no dollar amounts.

Grower placement fields
A grower's order responses carry exactly the published grower field list of yard names, hive counts, delivery dates and inspected strength, never beekeeper identities, pay or commission.

One-orchard inspection link
The broker emails an inspector one link that opens only that order's inspection sheet and is accepted by no other API.

Link expiry and replacement
An inspection link stops working with 410 once its report is signed, once a newer link is issued for the order, or once the lifetime set by INSPECTION_LINK_TTL_SECONDS passes, as qualified in Business rules.

Inspector opens the sheet
Opening the emailed link in a phone-sized browser shows the orchard's blocks, the yards delivered to each and the samples still needed, with no sign-in.

Server-computed block strength
Each block's average frames, pay tier and payable amount are computed on the server from its stored samples and returned with every sample change.

Safe frame photos
Frame photos are accepted only as JPEG, PNG or WebP judged by content, up to 8,000,000 bytes, stored under server-made keys, and never served as active content.

Short-lived file links
Photos and the signed report PDF are served only to the broker, the owning beekeeper, the orchard's grower and the live inspection link, through file links that expire.

Frame Odometer
When a sample changes a block, its average-frames digits roll column by column, the tier label and pattern swap after they settle, and the payable total rolls to the server amount, with the timing in Motion and effects.

Strength announcements and reduced motion
Every accepted strength change is announced in the "Strength readout" live region, and with reduced motion the figures change at once and a change note is added to the "Strength changes" log.

Inspector records samples
In the browser an inspector adds samples with photos, removes a mistaken one, and watches the block readout and payable total follow the server's figures, rolling back when a sample is refused.

All-or-nothing report signing
Signing a report stores its PDF, records the tier-adjusted balance invoice, marks the order and drops inspected and queues the grower's notice together, or does none of these.

Idempotent signing
Repeating a sign request with the same Idempotency-Key returns the first response and makes no second invoice, PDF or email, and the same key with a different body is refused with 409.

Signed report notice and PDF
A signed report sends the grower one notice email with each block's average, tier and payable amount and makes the report PDF available, with no beekeeper pay or commission in either.

Accepting and disputing inspections
A beekeeper accepts or disputes each inspected drop, the broker resolves a dispute to accepted, and every other transition is refused with 409.

Beekeeper reviews a drop
In the browser a beekeeper opens a drop, sees its photos and expected pay, and disputes it, and after the broker resolves it both see it accepted.

Exact settlement split
A settlement splits the orchard payable into the broker commission and each beekeeper's share in whole cents, summing exactly to the payable by the published largest-remainder rule.

Settlement recorded once
Settling records one grower payment in Kill Bill and marks the order settled, and repeats with the same key or a new key never record a second payment.

Queued settlement during billing outage
When Kill Bill is unreachable, settling answers 202 with the settlement queued, and it completes on its own within 30 seconds of billing returning, with no restart.

Broker settles an orchard
In the browser the broker reviews the settlement split, settles the orchard, and sees the ledger show it settled or queued with the matching copy.

Tiers not by colour alone
Each block on the plat map shows its tier by a written label and a distinct fill pattern as well as colour, explained by a legend.

Grower reviews the orchard
In the browser a grower opens their orchard, reads each block's tier and strength, opens a block's placements and the signed report, and sees no beekeeper pay or commission.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and nothing else is required to start the app.
/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package (the production tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) with version and licence, plus bundled fonts and icons.
Every shipped package is MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0 or 0BSD, and every bundled font is SIL Open Font License 1.1.
No datastore beyond the provided PostgreSQL and MinIO: no SQLite, Redis, embedded database or on-disk files used to keep application state.
The provided service configuration and seeded dev credentials are left untouched.
All application source is TypeScript, and a committed package-lock.json matches package.json.
No route, flag or environment switch exists only to change server state or the clock for testing.
